# Neonatal case fatality by birth-weight band

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Indicator ID | `neo_cfr_birth_weight` |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Status | Draft |
| Unit | Neonatal |
| Type | Outcome |
| Direction | Lower is better |
| Table | `qi.qi_neonatal_case_fatality_by_birth_weight`, one row per site and admission month |

## Definition

The share of neonates who died before discharge, among those whose outcome is known, reported separately for each birth-weight band.

## Numerator

Neonates who died before discharge (outcome "Dead"). Column: `deaths`.

## Denominator

Neonates discharged alive or who died (outcome "Alive" or "Dead"). Column: `known_outcome`.

## Exclusions

- Referred, absconded and discharged against medical advice, because their fate is unknown. They are counted in unknown_outcome and reported next to the rate.
- Admissions without a usable admission date, which cannot be placed in a month.

## Documentation completeness

The share of admissions with a usable birth weight: all bands except not_recorded. The share with an unknown outcome is also reported.

## Breakdowns

- Birth-weight band: under 1000 g, 1000 to 1499 g, 1500 to 2499 g, 2500 g and over, and not recorded. A band edge belongs to the higher band (1000 g is in 1000 to 1499 g).

## REDCap fields

`outcome`, `birth_wt`, `birth_wt_units`, `date_adm`, `hosp_id`

## Why it matters

The headline outcome for neonatal units. Birth weight is the strongest predictor of neonatal death, so banding makes hospitals that admit more very small babies comparable with those that admit fewer.

See [indicator conventions](README.md): suppression, empty rates, implausible values and completeness.
